plan.understanding: Replace the continuous 10 mm cross-sectional corner blend around the rectangular loop with a 2 mm radius matching the other cross-sectional blends, without changing the loop's main in-plane corner radii.

subtasks.goal: Replace the unique complete outer r=10.0 mm blend loop with r=2.0 mm while retaining the imported solid as the base body. Identify the loop by its four 90-degree r=10 cylindrical faces and four r=10 toroidal faces, corroborated by circular-arc centers [-226.62,-348.409,583.515], [-173.62,-362.126,532.32], [-173.62,-481.183,87.995], [-226.62,-494.9,36.8], [-886.62,-494.9,36.8], [-939.62,-481.183,87.995], [-939.62,-362.126,532.32], and [-886.62,-348.409,583.515]. Do not use a defeaturing, fillet, offset-shell, or half-space operation. Instead, create eight finite additive filler solids: for each straight r=10 segment, extrude the local cross-sectional region lying between the existing r=10 arc and a tangent r=2 arc derived from the sharp intersection of its actual adjacent support surfaces; for each r=10 toroidal corner, revolve the corresponding bounded filler region around that corner's measured support-cylinder axis so the exposed surface is the required r=2 toroidal transition. Limit every filler to the existing tangent boundaries of its associated r=10 face, then boolean-union the eight fillers with the unchanged imported solid and refine only coincident seams. The new r=2 center loci must be derived by offsetting the actual adjacent supports by 2.0 mm, not by reusing the r=10 center path. Keep the adjacent planar faces and the measured r=50.0 and r=63.0 cylindrical corner families geometrically unchanged. Confirm one valid solid, no remaining r=10 cylindrical or toroidal member, and r=2.0 normal-section arcs continuously around the full loop. Preserve the measured bounding box min [-949.62,-506.698,26.8] and max [-163.62,-338.409,595.312].
